• Discover hundreds of easy, play-based activities.

• Learn when the help of a professional is beneficial.

• Rest easy knowing all our advice is backed by rigorous research, providing reliable knowledge at your fingertips.

Bringing a new life into this world is a magical experience - there's no question about that. But it also brings with it a whirlwind of changes, particularly for first-time parents.

The days of poring over manual records and relying solely on maternal instincts are long behind us, with technology now offering a helping hand through every stage of the child-rearing process, right from pregnancy to parenting the toddler years.

In this post, we'll walk you through the best apps for new parents - designed to streamline your daily tasks, ease your anxieties, and create the reassuring sense of community that every parent needs.

## Why You Should Download a Few New Apps

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/5f9e3058e3ecc6040724fa97/66184f11b5c3259561969ce3_0-XAHu9EqokYlKWqdY9EbyWxiXb0SQr2DiZ2YbHgSCOqHavvAWRFIkdR9raiYDEJBqz6Hd105hw9I2Nqysztg8GWBvcSrwrIHNbU5HZa7zjJHerZWQBAVgiXUJ_rLpe3ekFUJ3XoFG4PHybQJ4ZMex4.png)

When it comes to parenting, the phrase "it takes a village" isn't just a saying - it's a modus operandi. Whether it's for tracking feeding times, decoding developmental milestones, or just finding a like minded community, new parents can benefit significantly from the right set of apps.

With smartphone use increasing substantially over the years, it only makes sense to digitize parenting in a way that's not just convenient but also intuitive and supportive.

### Get Immediate Assistance and Answers to Your Questions

In those frantic moments of your baby crying inconsolably or a mysterious rash appearing, an app with a direct line to expert advice is a godsend.

These platforms not only provide the answers you need at a swipe but can also connect you with pediatricians and specialists for in-depth consultations.

### Help You Track Feedings and Sleep

The days blend into one another with sleep-deprived hazes, but keeping a digital log of feedings and sleep patterns can help you spot trends and make sure your little one is healthy and on track.

### Keep an Eye on Developmental Milestones

In the blur of early parenthood, it’s easy to lose track of your baby’s development. An app that details what to expect and when can both reassure and inform parents about their child’s growth.

### Record Memories

From the first smile to the first steps, [every milestone deserves to be remembered](https://www.getearlybird.io/blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-finding-the-right-app-to-record-family-stories) and cherished. Apps like [EarlyBird](https://www.getearlybird.io/) that help you keep track of these moments are invaluable in creating a lasting record of your child's formative years.

### Access Educational Materials

With volumes of information out there, finding the best pearls of parenting wisdom can be a chore without a guiding hand.

Many apps curate and provide essential reading material that's just a download away. You can learn about anything and everything, from why your toddler is doing that weird nose picking thing to how to have those difficult conversations with your mother in law.

Navigating the early stages of parenthood brings a host of new responsibilities, among which is securing your child's financial future, and [EarlyBird](https://a.mmin.io/platform-click?utm_source=moneymade&utm_campaign=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.getearlybird.io%2F&utm_medium=platform-text&sid=user_1bcbfc08-1136-1404-1e03-1a0dca20241b&frameId=mm-widget_142b2606-146b-1af8-1e38-13bd5bbf0316&hash=6ca7f8eb660964c3e6559d93cf3b1abf&utm_content=textLinkClick&slug=earlybird2&eventLabel=815ce187-ed53-4d0e-ac20-293e450368e6) empowers you to establish a robust investment account for your little one, complete with a $15 bonus to start building wealth as they grow.

- **Save 3x more by including family and friends**

- **Expertly-crafted and diversified portfolios built for families**

Get Started

### Build a Sense of Community

Talking to others who have experienced - or are currently experiencing - what you're going through can offer a level of empathy and understanding that's hard to find anywhere else. Many apps have built-in features that allow you to connect with other parents around the world (or even right in your hometown).

### Improve Communication

Sometimes, it’s tricky to keep all caregivers on the same page. Apps that sync data and communication can ensure that every caretaker, from mom to dad to grandma and even the daycare teacher, has the exact information they need about the baby’s schedule and needs.

### Boost Organization and Time Management

From tracking vaccinations to planning the day's activities, an app can make sure that you're in control, always with a handle on what needs to be done.

## Tips for Choosing the Best App as a New Parent

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/5f9e3058e3ecc6040724fa97/66184f1125967eeb19675083_-Scj2nRZAr7mSWsB4EFBlz72V0sb6vsbwJdu8joM_sLQQXuO6zfYP6gWMygTzjIzjC5X23H14GeWEH2IT52tBa8IE4t73D89ggDQnXu5I047IPBGNmTREPALvLrXVGflFxfxtgcrBOLWZG5XwIHuqLA.png)

Before you start downloading every app that promises to make baby care easier, consider these tips to find the best fit for you and your family's needs.

### Consider the Learning Curve

You're likely to be wrestling with sleep deprivation, so look for apps with an intuitive design that doesn't require a NASA scientist to decode.

### Read the Reviews

Real-world parents can provide insight into the app’s benefits and drawbacks. Pay attention to what they say to avoid any unpleasant surprises post-installation.

### Look for Customization

Babies are as varied as the parents who raise them. An app that caters to your individual schedule and baby's needs will be far more useful than a generic one-size-fits-all platform.

### Check for Live Support

Immediate access to medical professionals can provide peace of mind when you're dealing with common concerns or need a second opinion.

### Opt for Synchronization with Multiple Devices

If you'll share caregiving duties, a seamless experience across all devices can keep everyone in the loop without the need for constant updates.

### Think About Longevity

The best apps are those that will grow with you and your child, offering support not just in the newborn days but also for toddlers and beyond.

## Best Apps for New Parents

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/5f9e3058e3ecc6040724fa97/66184f11606d4ab1ba2dbf7c_wgGsBsZ1MZu-Cj_2h3B1o0lnLLp-zDTbqGocIi6-DYHzj4sWDCqKy7VuPgxU02ecYt6OjVF2pfsniet0X-mKqjJXxHaGny1HDeYY4aFYx_Z-_Qv1U7rxZi2phCxeQDoR2NclzNjqfYM9gHTBRv8d9Kc.png)

Now that you know what to look for (and why) here are some of the best apps you can choose from to support and guide you through the first precious years of early parenthood.

### 1\. EarlyBird

For new parents who want to create a digital time capsule for their child, EarlyBird is the app of choice.

It’s a secure and private space where you can [store memories](https://www.getearlybird.io/blog/why-saving-memories-is-important-for-your-childs-development), along with the ability for family and friends to add to it.

EarlyBird also includes a financial growth option, allowing family and friends to make digital investment in your child’s future. The app provides a seamless combination of sentimental and practical features to help you treasure these moments and secure the future.

### 2\. Summer Health

[Summer Health](https://summerhealth.com/) extends healthcare beyond the doctor’s office with its Everyday Care concierge service.

Offering personalized access to pediatricians and specialists 24/7, the app is designed to handle urgent issues and provide ongoing guidance.

In addition, it provides 1-on-1 support for areas like sleep, nutrition, and lactation, offering a holistic approach to child healthcare.

### 3\. Maple

Staying organized as a parent can be a gargantuan task, but with [Maple](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/maple-household-planner/id1551070188), organization becomes intuitive. It serves as a comprehensive household management app, from meal planning and shopping lists to family calendaring.

Maple’s AI-powered “Fast” feature takes much of the planning off your plate, making sure that you’re never caught off guard with your parenting and household duties - as a result, guaranteeing that your focus can be entirely on nurturing your growing family.

### 4\. Huckleberry

[Huckleberry](https://huckleberrycare.com/) is a true one-stop baby & parenting app. Designed to track and optimize your child's sleep, feeding, growth, nutrition, and much more, Huckleberry is a versatile companion for the exhaustive demands of parenthood.

Its SweetSpot feature intuitively predicts your child's next nap time, simplifying the complexities of the sleep schedule. It goes beyond the traditional baby tracker and offers expert guidance that grows with your child.

### 5\. Hatch

[Hatch](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hatch-sleep/id1158048301) offers a suite of products and a companion app to facilitate better sleep for your child (and yourself!).

With features to create the perfect sleep environment and guide your baby through healthy sleep patterns, Hatch is poised to be a welcome addition to any new parent’s toolkit. The Rest, Rest+, and Restore features adapt to your child’s specific sleep needs at different stages, offering both flexibility and support.

### 6\. SolidStarts

When it’s time to introduce solid foods to your child, you want to be informed and confident. [SolidStarts](https://solidstarts.com/) provides extensive information on the when, how, and what of feeding your child, including nutrition details, tips on preparation, and videos of real babies eating the foods.

Its paid subscription offers a robust tracking feature to personalize the experience of food introduction and identify any food-related issues early on.

### 7\. Dyper

While not a traditional parenting app, [Dyper](https://dyper.com/) provides efficient diapering and supply solutions for busy parents. It's all about making the essentials - diapers - simpler and more sustainable.

With an intuitive browsing interface and user-friendly checkout, the app ensures that you’re always stocked up on the necessities. It also offers exclusive access to collection launches and discounts, focusing on the convenience side of parenting apps.

### 8\. Nanit

[Nanit](https://www.nanit.com/) is the tool for parents who need more visibility into their baby’s sleep patterns.

Using computer vision, Nanit offers insights into how your baby is sleeping, including if they’re fussy, awake, or sleeping soundly.

HorizontalOffers \| Atrium

It’s a high-tech addition to the parental arsenal, allowing for better understanding and management of one of the most important areas of early childhood growth and development.

## The Takeaway

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/5f9e3058e3ecc6040724fa97/66184f11e5739ceb6c9bfb80_6okXIWpBHt5NEMhKKOgvul8KpZVjZ4NOMvF0Vz79DixQ1pYxQDXbgdVQcGbrf6MVHp0F9e6nBh2flIq1zWwI8RcskmID2UABygj-LRnovgNwXiZ3obfBDV58MFEUh4B7jFMbDW8HZnDT-ETRqPOlf5Y.png)

Remember, no app can replace the love, attention, and intuition that you as a parent can give. But that's not what these apps are for. They're not replacements, but friends.

Instead, look at these digital tools as allies that can help you find more time and energy to be present with your little one. If you're feeling overwhelmed, take a deep breath, and know that you're doing great.

# EarlyBird Education – Early Literacy Screening App

**By Heather L. Russo, MEd, MFA**

PBIDA members know that over 60% of Pennsylvania’s fourth graders are not reading at grade level. This fact makes it harder to find the 15-20% of students who have dyslexia. With so many struggling readers, how can teachers distinguish those who struggle due to a specific learning disability? What would really help is a way to screen all preschool students before they begin school formally, some kind of tool that could identify not only dyslexic students but could also indicate

![Student using EarlyBird-dyslexia screener](https://earlybirdeducation.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Student-using-EarlyBird-Dyslexia-Screener.jpg)

students would have difficulties in certain areas of reading. EarlyBird Education’s Early Literacy Screening App is one such screening device. It can be used to help identify learners with dyslexia as well as non-dyslexic learners who are struggling and can pinpoint which areas of reading are most troublesome for each learner. In addition, EarlyBird offers methodology for teachers and training.

When Carla Small was Executive Director of Innovation at the Digital Health Accelerator at Boston’s Children’s Hospital, she oversaw many projects that aim to improve people’s lives. The early literacy screening app, created by Dr. Nadine Gaab, a cognitive neuroscience researcher who currently teaches at the Harvard University Graduate School of Education, was one of those many projects that Carla managed. Dr. Gaab had collaborated with professors from Tufts University, Northwestern University, and MIT to do the foundational work upon which she could build the screener. Their work was the READ Study and was published in the journal of Developmental Science, 2017. Under Carla’s supervision the resultant screening app was vetted and underwent a three-year study with students nationwide to validate its efficacy. This particular project caught her eye because one of her children is dyslexic. Having experienced the complicated road to help her child, Carla knew that the opportunity to screen all children could make an incredible difference in many people’s lives.

At the start of the pandemic in early 2020, Carla left her position at the Digital Health Accelerator to co-found EarlyBird Education in partnership with Dr. Gaab and Dr. Yaacov Petscher, an Associate Director of the Florida Center for Reading Research (FCRR) and the Director of the Quantitative Methodology and Innovation Division at FCRR. In the past three years, despite the challenges of the pandemic, EarlyBird Education has been approved by many state Departments of Education as a research-based screening tool for dyslexia and reading difficulties. In its first year, it was used to assess over 20,000 students. Forty states have instituted a law requiring that schools have screening protocols in kindergarten to identify dyslexia. Pennsylvania currently doesn’t have a law requiring early screening.

How does the app screen children? It combines gamification, artificial intelligence, and brain science, and it doesn’t require reading. Children, ages 4-8, use a tablet to play an interactive 20-50-minute game in which they meet a variety of animal characters that take them through several challenges. The challenges assess the child’s performance in regard to six early literacy milestones:

- Phonological awareness
- Phonological short-term memory
- Rapid automatized naming
- Knowledge of letter names and the sounds they make
- Vocabulary
- Oral listening comprehension

The data generated from the app provides a comprehensive profile of the child’s strengths and weaknesses across all of these literacy and pre-literacy milestones. The app then directs the teacher to research-based resources to begin to address the areas of difficulty. Links to lesson plans, proven intervention techniques, and professional development videos give teachers additional support. Links to books and apps direct and inform parents. EarlyBird Education offers workshops as well and professional development opportunities outside of the classroom.

The EarlyBird Education’s screening app doesn’t provide a diagnosis of dyslexia, but it can flag students with propensities for dyslexia. The EarlyBird Technical Manual explains how the app arrives at a target for dyslexia. Students are flagged for dyslexia based on an EarlyBird algorithm that uses a weighted combination of subtests to predict whether they would perform poorly on the Phonological Processing subtest of the Kaufman Test of Educational Achievement (KTEA-3). Upon learning a child has been flagged, the teacher is given feedback on instruction and next steps.

Because traditional screening is time-consuming, requiring a teacher to work one-on-one with a student on a paper and pencil assessment, the app’s ability to allow students to work independently within a short amount of time is helpful. It also reaches more youth in a more focused way. For underserved children, whose families may not seek outside tutoring or additional testing, the app can identify those with risk for a learning disability and target how to help, giving teachers and parents valuable information on how to proceed.

Already EarlyBird Education’s Early Literacy Screening App is being used in 20 states. Both parents and schools can purchase the app through EarlyBird Education’s website. While Pennsylvania doesn’t have a screening law in place, EarlyBird Education’s screening app is currently being implemented in at least ten schools and organizations in the state. Beyond school districts, EarlyBird is now available at home. With EarlyBird Families, children can play the game in the convenience of their home, and parents receive a comprehensive report of their strengths and weaknesses and a private consultation with a literacy specialist to develop a next steps action plan. Ultimately, EarlyBird would like to see pediatricians use it during well-visits prior to the start of school since the emotional implications for students with unidentified and untreated dyslexia are significant. EarlyBird Education seeks to reach as many children as possible, as their website states, “with a proactive, preventive model – that identifies children at risk earlier than ever before – and allows for interventions in the window of greatest efficiency and efficacy,” that is, before school begins or at the start of kindergarten.

##### _This story was originally authored by Heather L. Russo, MEd, MFA, and posted on [pa.dyslexiaida.org](https://pa.dyslexiaida.org/earlybird-education-early-literacy-screening-app/)._

##### _Heather L. Russo is an English teacher who has taught in private and public schools and at the college level. She currently works at Kutztown Area High School and is one of the editors for the PBIDA Focus Blog._

## EarlyBird Review: Investing for Kids – Pros, Cons and Competitors

May 15, 2025  \|  By [Jennifer Cooper](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/author/jennifercooper/)

Disclaimer: This post may contain affiliate links or links from our advertisers where we earn a commission, direct payment or products. Opinions are the author's alone, and this content has not been provided by, reviewed, approved or endorsed by any advertiser. Information shared on this site is for entertainment purposes only and should not be considered as professional advice.

- [Share](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fmarriagekidsandmoney.com%2Fearlybird-review%2F&t=EarlyBird%20Review%3A%20Investing%20for%20Kids%20-%20Pros%2C%20Cons%20and%20Competitors "Share on Facebook")
- [Tweet](https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=EarlyBird%20Review%3A%20Investing%20for%20Kids%20-%20Pros%2C%20Cons%20and%20Competitors&url=https%3A%2F%2Fmarriagekidsandmoney.com%2Fearlybird-review%2F&via=AndyHillMKM "Share on X")
- Pin
- [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmarriagekidsandmoney.com%2Fearlybird-review%2F&title=EarlyBird%20Review%3A%20Investing%20for%20Kids%20-%20Pros%2C%20Cons%20and%20Competitors&summary=NOTE%3A%20EarlyBird%20has%20recently%20been%20acquired%20by%20Acorns.%20All%20customer%20accounts%20will%20officially%20close%20on%20June%2023.%20Baby%20Shower%2C%20birthday%2C%20even%20kindergarten%20graduation%3A%20every%20celebration%20in%20your%20child%E2%80%99s%20life%20includes%20gifts%21%C2%A0While%20toys%20and%20clothes%20delight&mini=true "Share on LinkedIn")

**NOTE: EarlyBird has recently been acquired by [Acorns](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/acornsearly). All customer accounts will officially close on [June 23](https://techcrunch.com/2025/05/15/acorns-acquires-family-wealth-and-digital-memory-platform-earlybird/).**

Baby Shower, birthday, even kindergarten graduation: every celebration in your child’s life includes gifts! While toys and clothes delight kids and parents, you and those close to you may also want to contribute to your kid’s future. In this EarlyBird App Review, you’ll learn how to easily set up and fund an investment account in your son’s or daughter’s name.

## Who is EarlyBird?

> “Last Christmas I spent $50 on a lego set for my godson that brought him approximately 13 seconds of happiness before being tossed into the mountain of gifts that already included two other lego sets. This year I spent $50 on his future and was also able to leave a video message!”
>
> – [iPhone App Store EarlyBird Reviewer](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/earlybird-invest-gift-grow/id1517808320?see-all=reviews)

CEO Jordan Wexler co-founded [EarlyBird](https://www.getearlybird.io/) in 2000 with Caleb Frankel after experiencing much the same situation with his own nephew. By simplifying the set-up, funding and investing process for parents, EarlyBird helps them plan for their kids’ financial futures.

But the real focus shows in the simple gift-giving design that lets loved ones easily add cash into this same custodial account. EarlyBird estimates that its gift feature triples the total amount a child will have in their account by the time it becomes their own.

From the answers to three simple questions, a child’s EarlyBird investment portfolio reflects the risk profile and other preferences selected by their parents. Each of the five possible portfolios contains a mix of stocks, bonds, or both.

Friends and family create Memories in the form of a short video to attach to their money gifts.

As a new addition, the Nest feature lets parents invite close friends and extended family to join a small, closed community for their child.

[Learn More About EarlyBird](https://www.getearlybird.io/)

## EarlyBird Review: Best Features

![earlybird investing review](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/earlybird-Review-Mobile-Layout.jpg)

### Easy For Parents To Use

EarlyBird provides an incredibly easy way to set up an investment account for your child. Once you feel comfortable that you’re ready, start with your own information. Fill in your:

- Name
- Phone number
- Email address
- Birthdate
- Residential address
- Social security number

Next, connect to your bank account, and then you can create accounts for each of your children – even for one on the way!

While these [UGMA (Uniform Gifts to Minors Act)](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/how-to-open-a-custodial-brokerage-account-with-vanguard/) custodial accounts don’t have to be used for educational expenses like a 529 does, they do introduce a fiduciary duty for you as a parent. This means that funds in them cannot be used for a child’s day-to-day expenses or for child support.

### Easy For Friends and Family To Give

We all know the feeling of wanting to launch a young person into a successful future. EarlyBird’s gift-giving features make it simple for those who love your child to invest along with you. Even before they’re born!

Selecting the right account to give to only requires a phone number. Givers walk through a few simple steps to pay money directly to the child’s account from their own bank account.

### Memories With Every Gift

Tying every present to a video greeting “Turns an impersonal cash gift into a lifelong memory!” in the words of a user review. The app becomes a repository of good wishes from throughout a young person’s life, not simply an investment account.

### Widely Respected Investment Company

EarlyBird selects its ETFs, or Exchange Traded Funds, from [BlackRock](https://www.blackrock.com/us/individual), the world’s largest asset manager. ETFs trade like individual stocks or bonds but each contains a diversified mix of shares, charge lower fees than mutual funds, and offer lower risk than individual stocks or bonds.

## EarlyBird Review: Areas for Improvement

### Monthly Fees

Fixed monthly fees currently sit at $5.99/month or $49.99/year. For a $10,000 account, this amounts to 0.72% or 0.5% annually.

Investment accounts often carry fees, but even small amounts add up and can affect returns. So compare them when choosing how best to invest for your child.

### Flexibility of Use

UGMA accounts become the sole property of your child at an age your state decides, usually between 18-21. As the parent of a baby, or young child, you might assume that your child will be the model of responsibility when they grow up.

A [529 account](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/529-college-savings-plan/) is held in your name, with your child as beneficiary, and the funds earmarked for education.

A young adult with a UGMA account, by contrast, might decide to spend their money in other ways. Not all kids go to college, so this might turn out for the best. But you won’t have any say over their spending choices.

Educating your child far in advance of this age sets the stage for making smart choices.

Also, keep in mind that assets owned by your child may reduce the amount of financial aid colleges offer by 20-25% of the asset value. Financial aid teams weight UGMA and custodial bank accounts more heavily than 529 plans.

### Projected Values Not Guaranteed

On average, over long periods of time, financial markets go up and so do your investments. However, deep dips in value sometimes occur as well. It can take years for investment portfolios to recover after one of these.

EarlyBird calculates projected values that use historical averages and compounding. Since these cannot be guaranteed, it’s important your child’s future assets include cash savings to cushion against the ups and downs of the stock and bond markets.

### Nest Concerns

Most kids today grow up in some type of social media spotlight. Parents differ in opinions on how best to navigate this with their little ones.

The Nest feature in EarlyBird provides a smaller setting to post videos and photos, since only people you invite to be in it can see them. EarlyBird encourages each person to post videos and photos – called Moments – to share with the child.

Parents add in Milestones – videos showing a first step, the first day of preschool, or a super cute baby-and-puppy nap day. The user interface then nudges each child’s EarlyBird Nest to respond to these parental videos. Instead of a like or emoji, they can select from one of three featured dollar amounts.

While this no doubt encourages more gifting, not all parents may feel comfortable having their child’s big accomplishments rated with a specific amount of cash. Their friends and family members may also prefer seeing cute videos that don’t come with a subtle ask for money.

Your family can choose to use, or not use, this feature in ways that fit with your own values.

## EarlyBird Review: Competitors

Other companies allow you to set up custodial accounts for your child without the monthly fee.

### Vanguard

[Vanguard](https://investor.vanguard.com/accounts-plans/ugma-utma) pioneered index funds and offers youth accounts and custodial accounts as well. If you already work with them for your own retirement, you may feel comfortable using their tools to set up an account for your child. With low ETF management fees, your assets will grow more quickly.

Here's a detailed article on how to set up a [custodial brokerage account with Vanguard](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/how-to-open-a-custodial-brokerage-account-with-vanguard/).

### Fidelity

[Fidelity](https://www.fidelity.com/open-account/custodial-account) likewise prides itself on low management fees in its ETFs and allows you to create similar custodial accounts under the UGMA/UGTA or 529 umbrellas.

Vanguard and Fidelity give you access to any asset for your child’s portfolio. If you’re new to investing, this might prove a bit daunting. But they both also offer suggested model investment mixes and educational materials and seminars.

## EarlyBird Review: FAQ

### Is EarlyBird App Legit?

EarlyBird started 5 years ago and has venture backing. It selects its ETFs from BlackRock, the world’s largest asset manager.

EarlyBird is a Registered Investment Advisor. As such, it holds a fiduciary responsibility to its clients and so must provide investment advice that is in its client’s best interest.

Apex Clearing Corporation acts as its brokerage partner, and its holdings are protected by the SIPC against fraud or brokerage failure up to $500,000. SIPC does not cover investments, however, against market losses.

### How Much Does the EarlyBird App Cost?

Parents pay monthly fees to EarlyBird. $5.99/month or $49.99/year.

### How Does EarlyBird Make Money?

EarlyBird earns fees every month from parents who hold custodial accounts for their kids.

## Final Thoughts on Our EarlyBird Review

★★★

EarlyBird makes investing in your child’s future easy and memorable. They designed their sites specifically to enable contributions from your family and close friends.

That being said, more established companies like Vanguard and Fidelity have improved their processes over the years to make investing for kids easier. And they offer custodial brokerage account service with no monthly fees.

If you’re looking for a way to jumpstart your child’s financial future, we would recommend working with either of those firms before EarlyBird. If you prefer convenience and simplicity and don't mind the monthly fees, EarlyBird could be the right solution for your [generational wealth investing](https://marriagekidsandmoney.com/podcast/generational-wealth-investing/) needs.
